items.summary: Says she will restore education standards and, using the Lieutenant Governor's seats on university and college boards, push to restore merit in admissions and protect academic standards.
items.title: Restore education standards and merit in college admissions

citations.quote: I will restore education standards, develop a bold economic plan that helps businesses thrive, rein in politicized commissions that have failed to protect our water, farmland, and way of life, defend Title IX for our daughters in sports, and fight antisemitism on our campuses.
Gloria will fight to restore merit in admissions, protect academic standards, and stop setting students up for failure.

items.summary: Authored legislation enacted in 2010 (Chapter 3 of the 5th Extraordinary Session) in response to the federal Race to the Top initiative, including the Open Enrollment Act, which lets pupils in 1,000 schools identified annually as low achieving apply to enroll in a higher-performing school anywhere in the state; a Senate committee analysis lists it under her name, and Irvine Unified School District policy calls these "Romero Bill transfers".
items.title: Open Enrollment Act (Chapter 3, Statutes of 2010, 5th Extraordinary Session)

citations.quote: California enacted legislation (Chapter 3 of the 5th Extraordinary Session, Statutes of 2010, Romero) in response to the federal Race to the Top initiative, including the Open Enrollment Act specific to pupils who attend low-achieving schools.

Allows any pupil enrolled in one of 1,000 schools identified annually by the Superintendent of Public Instruction (SPI) as low achieving to apply for enrollment in a higher performing school anywhere in the state.

Interdistrict transfer requests made pursuant to the Open Enrollment Act (“Romero Bill transfers”) shall only be approved by the Superintendent or designee in accordance with the provisions of this policy and its implementing regulations.
Romero authored landmark legislation such as the Parent Trigger and Open Enrollment Act, the first laws in the nation to give parents real authority over chronically failing schools.
